substantive_reconstruction.complex_complements: Put r=|c|, δ=1−r², u=(ψ−conj(c)φ)/sqrtδ and v=(φ−cψ)/sqrtδ. Direct inner-product expansion gives norms one, φ†u=0, ψ†v=0, ψ†u=φ†v=sqrtδ, and u†v=−c. In particular 1−conj(c)c is δ, not 1−c². These computations are valid for genuinely complex overlaps and use no rephasing assumption.
substantive_reconstruction.two_outcome_obstruction: For a positive effect E, zero expectation on a vector implies annihilation, by its positive square root. Hence an unambiguous Eψ annihilates φ and, on the stipulated two-dimensional span, equals a uu† with a≥0; similarly Eφ=b vv†. Completeness evaluated on ψ and φ forces aδ=bδ=1. Therefore tr(Eψ+Eφ)=2/δ>2, contradicting the trace of I. Equivalently self-adjoint Eψ with Eψψ=ψ and Eψφ=0 would force c=0. This rules out every valid conclusive-only two-effect measurement, not merely one guessed pair.
substantive_reconstruction.three_effect_validity: For the supplied weights 1/(1+r), form F=[u v]. Its Gram matrix F†F has eigenvalues 1±r, and F is invertible because r<1. Thus S=(uu†+vv†)/(1+r) has eigenvalues 1 and (1−r)/(1+r), so it is a positive contraction. P?=I−S is positive with eigenvalues 0 and 2r/(1+r); all three effects sum to I. Wrong-label expectations vanish, correct-label probability is δ/(1+r)=1−r for either input, and inconclusive probability is r. At r=0 a two-outcome orthogonal measurement is possible; r=1 is excluded and the given complement formula is undefined.
